newsitem.title: UK: Tesco up as investors seek defensive stocks.
newsitem.headline: Tesco up as investors seek defensive stocks.

text.p: Shares in Tesco Plc led a sector-wide food retailers rally on Tuesday, bucking the broadly weaker trend in UK shares as investors sought so-called defensive stocks, dealers said.

By 1311 GMT, Tesco shares were up seven pence to 407-1/2p, having reached a new high for the year at 410p earlier. The FTSE 100 share index was down 47.4 points at 4,763.3 amid concerns about rising interest rates and a further appreciation in sterling.
Elsewhere in the sector, shares in ASDA Group Plc were up 2-1/4p to 137p, while shares in J. Sainsbury Plc added 6-1/2p to 386p. Safeway Plc climbed four pence to 371-1/2p.

"The market in general is getting hit by worries about interest rates and the currency, but the food retailers are domestic earners - they're not currency sensitive and not as interest rate sensitive," said one dealer.
Earlier, stronger-than-expected UK retail price data reinforced the view that the Bank of England will raise interest rates at Wednesday's policy meeting.
That sent sterling through 2.97 German marks, which weighed on shares in companies with significant exposure overseas.
Dealers were expecting more currency-related profit downgrades for big multinationals and said risk-adverse investors were switching into stocks less affected by those factors.
